analysis.title: Developed Markets: Q3.2026 Earnings Season Monitor (Azimut Global View, 2 Nov 2026)
key_insights: Q3 2026 earnings are coming in above consensus. Reported EPS growth is +19% y/y in the U.S. and +34% y/y in Europe, implying EPS surprise factors of +3% and +13%. Japan's net profit is -3% y/y, a -2% surprise.
Reporting progress: 55% of U.S. companies, 49% of European companies and 18% of TSE Prime companies have reported.
U.S.: 81% of reporting companies beat EPS estimates and 60% beat sales estimates. Sales growth is +11% with a +2% surprise, and all eleven sectors posted positive top-line growth.
U.S. EPS growth is led by Information Technology (+27% y/y), Industrials (+41%) and Energy (+168%). Seven of eleven sectors show double-digit EPS growth, Healthcare is flat and Real Estate is +3%.
The report says broadening of earnings growth beyond a few sectors is finally taking hold in the U.S. and Europe, with most sectors posting double-digit EPS growth.
Price reactions to U.S. earnings are skewed negative. Beats earned a median +0.2% 1-day move relative to the market, and misses a median -1.0%.
U.S. blended Q3 2026 S&P 500 EPS estimate rose from $81.40 at the January lows to $90.60. FY26 EPS growth consensus is 34.8% (from 15.6% in January) and FY27 growth is 17.5%.
Europe: STOXX 600 revenue growth is +14%, 1% above consensus. 52% of companies beat sales and 56% beat EPS. Ten of eleven sectors posted positive sales growth.

Europe EPS growth is led by Energy (+126% y/y). Ex-Energy growth is +17%, with eight of the remaining ten sectors at double-digit growth. IT is +42%, Discretionary +28%, Staples +17%, Utilities +3% and Communication Services +3%.
Europe's aggregate EPS growth is ahead of the U.S. in aggregate and median terms (+13% y/y vs +10% y/y per the report), helped by a weaker euro that lifted relative sales beats.
European price reactions are also negatively skewed: beats got a median +0.5% relative 1-day gain and misses -2%.
U.S. Cyclicals are delivering much stronger EPS growth than Defensives (+29% y/y vs +10%). European Defensives' beat rate has rebounded toward its highest since 2022.

Japan: 45% of reporting TSE Prime companies beat net profit estimates and 59% beat revenue estimates. Revenue growth is +14% y/y while net profit is -3%. Twelve of sixteen sectors show positive earnings growth.
Japan sector spread: Pharmaceuticals +293% y/y, Foods +136%, Commercial & Wholesale +46%. Electric Power & Gas is -153%, Defensive segments -42% and Autos & Transportation -19%.

Consensus FY26 EPS growth has been revised up to 18.7% for STOXX 600 (24.0% for the Eurozone) and to 22.0% for Topix (from 11.1% in January), with FY27 Topix growth at 10.7%. European upgrades were concentrated in Energy, Semis and Materials.

Transcript analysis: demand mentions 88% positive, margins 74% positive, macro 43% negative, FX 40% positive for European exporters. Input costs were 82% negative on elevated energy prices and interest rates 60% negative.
Guidance mentions were 62% positive and 34% neutral. Capex commentary was 58% positive and 35% neutral. Buyback sentiment was 91% positive and dividend sentiment 82% positive.

Microsoft: Azure grew 48% in constant currency and M365 Commercial Cloud 18%. The fiscal Q2 guide is Azure 49-50% and M365 Commercial 19%. FY26 capex was trimmed from $175B to $170B, attributed to compute deployment delays rather than weaker AI demand.

Alphabet: GAAP EBIT missed by 6.3%, entirely from margin compression in Google Services. Google Cloud beat on revenue and EBIT, and TPU sales are teased from 2027. Management reiterated its $195B-$205B framework.

Amazon: operating income beat by 7%, and retail cost-to-serve fell enough to absorb an $880M fuel and linehaul headwind. AWS revenue growth of 39.3% y/y was below investor expectations, but management projects growth above 40% in 2027 and 2028.

Meta: Family of Apps revenue grew 26% y/y (2% above consensus) with a 35% operating margin excluding legal charges, and the Q4 guide was above the Street. The new 'Muse' product reached 10M+ users in six weeks with 25% daily usage.

Apple: revenue was $114.5B (+12% y/y) with diluted EPS of $2.10 and gross margin of 47.9%, helped by tariff refunds. December-quarter revenue guide is +8.5% y/y, and gross margin guidance softened because about $1B in expected tariff refunds did not materialize. Services growth slowed to 10%.

Asset allocation: Developed Market equities were upgraded back to Neutral. The report says the move reflects relative value versus bonds after bonds outperformed over two weeks, not an outright positive view on stocks. Further equity declines are possible, and the end of the U.S. midterm elections should remove an uncertainty.

Emerging Market equities were also upgraded to Neutral. Caution factors are hawkish central banks and souring sentiment on technology stocks. Positives are a wide valuation discount to developed markets, hyperscaler capex exposure and sector rotation.

Developed Market sovereign bonds were tactically cut to Neutral after the pullback in yields, especially at the long end. The long-term view on bonds is unchanged, the report favors the belly of the curve, and it aims to rebuild positions if rates rise again.

Credit and EM debt: Slightly Underweight on Developed Market corporate bonds (spreads widened since mid-September but are not yet attractive, investment grade preferred over high yield) and on Emerging Markets Debt. Commodities stay Slightly Overweight: tactically cautious on precious metals, constructive on industrial metals and rare earths. USD, EUR, CNY and other EM currencies are Neutral.

earnings_insights: Q3 2026 U.S. (S&P 500, 55% reported): reported EPS +19% y/y, aggregate surprise +3% vs consensus, 81% beat EPS, sales +11% y/y with a +2% surprise, 60% beat sales.
Q3 2026 Europe (STOXX 600, 49% reported): reported EPS +34% y/y, surprise +12% to +13%, 56% beat EPS, revenue +14% y/y and 1% above consensus.
Q3 2026 Japan (TSE Prime, 18% reported, July-September quarter): net profit -3% y/y, surprise -2%, 45% beat net profit estimates, revenue +14% y/y.

Blended S&P 500 Q3 2026 EPS consensus estimate is $90.60, up from $81.40 in January. Consensus FY26 EPS growth is 34.8% and FY27 is 17.5%. STOXX 600 FY26 EPS growth estimate is 18.7% and Topix FY26 is 22.0%.
Microsoft fiscal Q1 (reported): Azure +48% CCY, M365 Commercial Cloud +18% CCY. The fiscal Q2 guide is Azure 49-50% CCY and M365 Commercial 19% CCY.
Alphabet Q3 (reported): GAAP EBIT missed consensus by 6.3%. Cloud revenue and EBIT beat.
Amazon Q3 (reported): operating income beat by 7%, and AWS revenue growth was 39.3% y/y.
Meta Q3 (reported): Family of Apps revenue +26% y/y (2% above consensus), 35% operating margin excluding legal charges.
Apple fiscal Q4 (reported): revenue $114.5B (+12% y/y), diluted EPS $2.10, gross margin 47.9%. December-quarter revenue growth guide is +8.5% y/y.

macro_indicators.reading: Could reach the lowest level since 2010
macro_indicators.interpretation: The report's calendar says rising mortgage rates could push sales to a 16-year low. The data release is dated 04.11 in its Main Events grid.

macro_indicators.reading: Above 4% would cement expectations of another ECB rate hike in December
macro_indicators.interpretation: A reading above 4% would support expectations of an ECB hike in December.

macro_indicators.reading: Job growth expected to stay modest
macro_indicators.interpretation: Tighter immigration is slowing population growth, which limits job gains.

macro_indicators.reading: October inflation expected to be more moderate after peaking in September
macro_indicators.interpretation: Inflation is expected to ease from the September peak.

risk_factors: Rising input costs (82% negative mentions, tied to elevated energy prices) and rising interest rates (60% negative) are emerging earnings headwinds.
Hawkish stance of many central banks.
Souring investor sentiment on technology stocks, which carry the largest weight in emerging market indices.
Further equity declines are possible while weakness persists, and rates may rise again.
Macro sentiment in earnings calls is 43% negative.
Developed Market credit spreads widened since mid-September but are not yet considered attractive.
vol_and_positioning: Equity market weakness persists per the report, so caution remains warranted and further declines are possible.
Price reactions to Q3 earnings are skewed negatively in the U.S. and Europe: beats are rewarded modestly and misses penalized more heavily.
geopolitical: U.S. midterm elections are a major source of market uncertainty, and their conclusion is expected to support equities.
cross_bank_references: Charts and earnings data are sourced from J.P. Morgan.
Transcript analysis sourced from AlphaSense and Barclays research.

tension_points.bull_case: Once the U.S. midterm elections are over, a main source of uncertainty falls away, and the ongoing sector rotation is underpinning the major indices.
tension_points.bear_case: Equity weakness persists, further declines are possible, and bonds outperformed over the past two weeks. Hawkish central banks and souring tech sentiment add caution.
tension_points.what_invalidates: Further equity declines while weakness persists would keep caution warranted. A rise in rates would prompt the report to rebuild bond positions.
